decisions: Gate BOTH halves (externref paint + the query_function no-return carry) and the vendored Win32 name list behind one option: each half alone can change emitted C on some target, so one gate is what buys the reviewable 'option off => byte-identical everywhere' guarantee.

Carry externref in the symbol-table PROPERTY MAP rather than porting ExternRefSymbol: the import FunctionSymbol's map entry is 1 byte (min_funcsymbol_size), so a pointer-width slot read never finds it as a container and always takes queryProperties' property branch; externref is read in exactly one place in the workspace, so the blast radius is bounded. Mapping a second (ExternRef) symbol at the slot would change naming/typing there and would break query_function's `is_function` requirement.

Vendor upstream's PEFunctionsThatDoNotReturn as its OWN file matched on the PE/COFF arm instead of widening kuna's merged PeMacFunctionsThatDoNotReturn: upstream keeps the PE and Mach-O sets separate, and the added names are Windows-only, so merging further would match ExitProcess/KeBugCheck against a Mach-O. kuna's Mach-O list is still missing upstream's Mach-O names -- a separate, out-of-scope gap.

Default-ON: 0/675 datatest assertions change with the flip, speed is within budget (negative whole-binary), no function is gained or lost on either PE, gotos never increase, and every non-PE target is byte-identical. DIV-57.

The triage record's filed mechanism (a new P2 pass matching a CALLIND through a global) was REFUTED before any code was written: at the P2 flow seam the CALLIND target is a free unique temp and raw flow IR carries no def-use links, so the backward walk it needs is unavailable.

SECOND FINDING, not in the brief: Database::build_global_query copied a FunctionSymbol's inject_id but not its no_return into the GlobalEntry snapshot, so Architecture::query_function returned is_no_return()==false for every callee and FuncCallSpecs::deindirect always took its lateRestriction success path WITHOUT scheduling a restart - the CALLIND->CALL rewrite happened in place and the already-walked flow was never recomputed. Naming the call was necessary but not sufficient; this is the half that fixes the boundary. Proved by A/B (externref alone leaves the whole absorbed body, even under an explicit `option noreturn ExitThread`), not inferred.
